Senses.Explanation: Water does not wash water states that a thing does not act upon itself as a second object. The records pair it with gold not exchanging for gold and mind not seeing mind, then turn the formula into a direct question at the teaching seat. Baizhang explains the formula beside non-seeking and unobstructed understanding; Hongzhi coordinates water, gold, eyes, and mind; Fuan Kefeng and Rifang demand that the assembly supply the line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 胸跣足；歷代祖師出了不肯入，到處赤手白拈。月掌這裏，山門佛殿長年蕩蕩地，總沒絲毫障隔，入也繇你入、出也繇你出，只是不許踢著門檻。」喝一喝，云：「有甚麼限？」因事，上堂。僧問：「峰頭翻玉浪，額下隱明珠，蓋覆不來即不問，面門出入事如何？」師云：「菴居冷淡僧頻走。」僧云：「漁翁釣得江心月，特地拈來便請觀。」師云：「這裏不著殘羹餿飯。」僧云：「恁麼則滿目青山，一塵不點。」師打，云：「將謂孤負汝。」乃云：「古木參天向上句，相逢不拈出；平橋跨水截流機，舉意便知有。碧落亭下，涼沁心源；浣香洞口，寒生毛骨。塵中行客、方外高人，驀地到來，煩喧頓息。盡道南天方廣、北地清涼，總莫逾此。便擬拈提大小石頭，品頌日月佛面，不知早被法雷閣刺透耳門、漾月池浸爛腳板了也。大眾！此是山僧真實告報，汝若放得下去，等閒穿過竹廊，自有一轉、兩轉相為處；或更怖頭狂走、向外馳求，玲瓏嵒斷不點頭招手、掣袖鉤衣。何故聻？留得五湖明月在，不愁無處下金鉤。」小參。「達磨隻履鬧中拋下，東天也到，西天也到；神光一臂冷地揮落，左手也著，右手也著。將心與汝安，北斗面南看；與汝安心竟，獼猴照古鏡。易得諸佛法印，難覓自己身心，唯須息見，不用求真。若道水不洗水，金不博金，莫將閒學解，埋沒祖師心。」檀越請上堂。「把得定，古佛風規十方通暢；打得開，祖師關捩大地全收。月掌院裏上堂，暹羅國裏打鼓，驚發東海龍王助佛揚化之心，向虛空中轟個霹靂，於水面上捲陣涼風，便見梁朝傅大士、楚國孟嘗君，鬚髯戢戢、襟袖蕭蕭，倒橐傾箱和盤托入，直得齋廚與漆桶爭光、杓柄共茶銚鬥力，一缽三鐼後，個個飽膨脝，不知天之高、地之厚，又何暇顧日月星辰之流轉、山川草木之凋零？且道何緣得到與麼地？」良久，云：「秋風入戶自生涼，流水到門非有意。」上堂。「祖師血脈、諸佛心髓、聲聞緣覺、天堂地獄、人畜草芥、有情無情，天左旋、地右轉，南斗六、北斗七。」豎拂子，云：「總在這裏。只這個，亦能殺人、亦能活人，殺人不用殺人刀、活人不用活人劍。大眾！作麼生見個不用底道理？道得底，出來對眾道看；道不得……」擊拂子，云：「一擊百雜碎，從教遍界分身。」老和尚送法衣到，上堂。拈香，云：「此一瓣香，量超空界，轉空界而透法身；價逾大千，遍大千而作佛事。爇向爐中，專申供養始祖釋迦文佛。伏願天回聖瑞，地轉嘉祥，人人悟涅槃玅心，各各開正法眼藏。」次拈香，云：「此一瓣香，熏透飲光鼻孔，直下穿來；爍開於密腦門，從空迸出。供養禪宗第一祖
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB306.xml). Neishao Zhizhong makes a present hall teaching of this line; an inherited first utterance stays earlier.

Occurrences.Kwic: 。嶽云：『修證即不無，污染即不得。』難出鬼窟家鄉。祖云：『即此不污染，諸佛所護念。汝既如是，我亦如是。』誤賺幾多人。又，二祖神光問達磨云：『諸佛法印可得聞乎？』舉心即錯，動念即乖。磨云：『諸佛法印不從人得。』你來東土作麼？光云：『我心未安，乞師與安。』潑油救火。磨云：『將心來，與汝安。』慣會就窠打劫。光云：『內外覓心了不可得。』什麼所在去了？磨云：『我與汝安心竟。』且信一半。所以三世諸佛歷代祖師，實無一法與人，只解解粘去縛，使箇箇獨脫無依，人人自繇自在。今有將佛祖言教以為宗旨，密室商量，遞相傳授，他日閻羅面前，喫鐵棒有日在。不見巖頭云：『若將實法與人，土也難消。』」拈拄杖云：「大眾！且道：者箇是實法耶？非實法耶？若道是實法，土也難消。若道非實法，茫茫業識。還委悉麼？此處不能明實際，他年怎透死生關？」卓一卓，下座。上堂。「十方無壁落，四面亦無門，杲日正當空，內外悉明徹。過去諸佛、現在諸佛、未來諸佛，各各住於本位，山自青、水自綠、松自直、棘自曲，未嘗變易一絲毫。秪如諸佛出世、祖師西來，更為甚麼事？忽有師僧聞恁麼道，呵呵大笑而退。山僧即喚維那，明窗下安排。何故？不見道伶俐衲僧難得。」上堂。「水不洗水，金不博金，雨下地濕，日出天晴。釋迦老子，雪山受了六年饑凍，徒自苦辛。明星現時，似乎證入，卻也未真。臨濟大師三度於黃檗處問佛法的的大意，三度被打，忍氣吞聲。且道：極則一句又作麼生？」卓拄杖云：「碧岫雲生。」上堂。「有水皆含月，無山不帶雲。壺公瓢子裏，別有一乾坤。若也知消息，歸家罷問程。所以道，其住也，坐斷天下老和尚舌頭；其去也，千人萬人羅籠不住。到者裏，更須知有照用同時、人境俱奪始得。」上堂。「迷之原無失，悟之原無得。得失既忘懷，扶桑耀紅日。」喝一喝，下座。上堂。「威音那畔、空劫已前者一著子，未嘗動著一絲毫，及乎萬姓紛紜、千差顯露者一著子，亦未嘗動著一絲毫，只貴伶俐漢子直下承當，便能得大受用。苟或三撘不回，豈免沉迷苦海？秪如龍潭吹滅紙燈處，德山見甚道理，便爾自肯？蝦蟆吞大虫。」上堂。「釋迦掩室於摩竭，淨名杜口於毘耶，明明鬼窟藏身。普慧雲興二百問，普賢瓶瀉二千酬，要且葛藤不少。直饒二途不涉，別有出身之路，正好朝打三千，暮打八百。秪如古德云：『你有拄杖子，與你拄杖子；你無拄杖子，奪卻你拄杖子。』大眾！既無拄杖子，又奪箇甚麼？千古萬古黑漫漫，填溝塞壑無人會。」上堂。「一大藏教是箇切腳正文，從來無人讀著

Occurrences.Kwic: 養，未有休日。且道正當恁麼時，落在什麼處？」晚參，舉：「陸亙大夫問南泉：『弟子家中有一片石，有時坐、有時臥，欲鐫作佛，得不？』泉云：『得。』陸云：『莫不得不？』泉云：『不得。』雲巖云：『坐則佛，不坐則非佛。』洞山云：『不坐則佛，坐則非佛。』」師云：「轉功就位，轉位就功，還他洞上父子。且道南泉意作麼生？直是針錐不得。」晚參，舉：「佛前有一女子入定，佛敕文殊出定，殊乃運神力托上梵天出定不得，佛乃云：『下方罔明大士能出此定。』須臾，罔明至，敕令出定，罔明彈指三下，女子便出定。」師云：「若定若動，當人變弄，鴻毛輕而不輕，太山重而非重。還知老瞿曇鼻孔在我手裏麼？」晚參，舉：「雪峰與三聖行次，見一隊猢猻，峰云：『秖者猢猻各各背一面古鏡。』聖云：『歷劫無名，何以彰為古鏡？』峰云：『瑕生也。』聖云：『一千五百人善知識，話頭也不識。』峰云：『老僧住持事繁。』」師云：「當時若見雪峰道：『瑕生也。』但近前云：『喏喏！』且道何故如此？爭之不足，讓之有餘。」晚參，舉：「法眼問覺上座：『船來？陸來？』覺云：『船來。』眼云：『船在甚麼處？』覺云：『船在河裏。』覺退，眼問傍僧云：『你道適來者僧具眼不具眼？』」師云：「水不洗水，金不博金，昧毛色而得馬，靡絲絃而樂琴，結繩畫卦有許事，喪盡真淳太古心。」晚參，舉：「曹山問德上座：『佛真法身猶若虛空，應物現形如水中月，作麼生說箇應底道理？』德云：『如驢覷井。』山云：『道則太煞道，只道得八成。』德云：『和尚又如何？』山云：『如井覷驢。』」師云：「驢覷井，井覷驢，智容無外，淨涵有餘，肘後誰分印？家中不蓄書。機絲不挂梭頭事，文彩縱橫意自殊。」晚參，舉：「長慶示眾云：『淨潔打疊了，近前就我索，驀脊與你一棒。有者棒到你，你須具大慚愧；若無者一棒到你，你向甚麼處會？』」師云：「開口喫常住飯，展腳臥長連床，求箇知慚愧者難得。還知長慶棒落處麼？雷開蟄戶電燒尾，引出崢嶸頭角來。」晚參，舉：「黃檗示眾云：『汝等諸人盡是噇酒糟漢，與麼行腳何處有今日？還知大唐國裏無禪師麼？』僧云：『只如諸方匡徒領眾又作麼生？』檗云：『不道無禪，只是無師。』」師云：「岐分絲染太勞勞，葉綴花聯敗祖曹，妙握司南造化柄，水雲器具在甄陶。屏割繁碎，剪除氄毛，星衡藻鑑，玉尺金刀。黃檗老！察秋毫，坐斷春風不放高。」晚參，舉：「雲巖問道吾：『大悲菩薩用許多手眼作麼？』吾云：『如人夜間背手摸枕子。』巖云：『我會也。』吾云：『汝作麼
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J32/J32nB272.xml). Hongzhi Jue makes a own case comment of this line; an inherited first utterance stays earlier.

Occurrences.Kwic: 門。閒田地上松風，田庫奴不知狼籍我多少？家無小廝，不成君子，簑衣箬笠，天晴時甚人曬㫰？斷頭船子下揚州，洪浪巨濤裏看風使帆，阿誰識得？李三黑一生只賣炭，雖然汙我清白家聲，泠地裏全承渠力，年來失錢遭罪，也須大家著隻眼。法堂草深丈許，我總不憂，秪憂太陽溢目，萬里不掛片雲，青天也須喫棒。時有目者不見，忽然南山起雲、北山下雨，溪深杓柄長，如何去取？三伏毒熱，井底冰生，鑊湯爐炭裏安居底，阿師還曾念我？赤骨律寒毛卓豎，俯仰乾坤無可告語，有懷如許，不審立業成家者作何料理？」「貧無卓錐，動容揚古路；富有四海，遍界不能藏。既藏不得，則從日炙風吹，隨波逐浪，或截流而渡，夾岸鳴榔；或深入不毛，千江釣雪。布帆明月，贏得夢貼蘆花；起倒黑甜，忘卻故鄉水草。無位真人行一步，過無量恒沙世界，未出渠儂毛孔；舒一光，蔽百千日月朗耀，不得其門而入。璣上座今日將其門洞啟，直令渠全身出現，普使群生萬有眼見耳聞、舌嘗鼻嗅、身觸意思，縱饒六根不具、八識不全者，一點也背渠不得。東山門下繇來火烈風嚴，間不容髮，而今覿面提持，如何迴避？若也避得，莫謂天台路嶮巇，羊腸更在青霄上；若避不得，相見易為好，共住難為情。」「家貧猶自可，路貧愁殺人。水不洗水，金不博金。江南塞北，月泠風高；東魯西秦，山深水闊。四衢道上磚，片片皆硬，開口告人難；大千沙界草，莖莖是藥，把手將不去，寒暑迭遷。解忌口者，一牛飲水，五馬不嘶；不解忌口者，求生不得，求死不得。未審我無上醫王，如何救療？」「昔日世尊，於涅槃會上，普告眾曰：『吾有正法眼藏，涅槃妙心，付囑摩訶迦葉。』若論正法眼藏，人人取之不竭，用之無窮，大千世界，無絲毫許障隔。涅槃妙心，圓明清淨，應物現形，放之則彌漫八極，卷之則匿跡韜光，在聖不增，處凡不減，因甚又道付囑摩訶迦葉？」「車不橫推，理無曲斷，雖則法爾如然，其奈絃急則促。文殊、普賢各各翻轉面皮，主人公二俱不受，情與無情，異口同音，曰：『官不容針，私通車馬。』觀音大士從聞、思、修入三摩地，曰：『某甲罪過。』長汀子於十字街頭呵呵大笑，曰：『口秪堪喫飯。』是則固是，忽有人拈起一粒，問云：『這箇從甚處得來？』又作麼生？」「好雨點點，不落在別處，無問情與無情，靡不承其恩力。其如根器匪一，弗克含藏，流而為泉、為澗、為沼、為池、為江漢、為河海，蹄涔溝澮無不有之，彼彼自深自滿，洋溢波濤，莫知源之所自。爰有一人截流而渡，指目彼岸此岸異派中流，既而舟航競作，往復無時，蕩蕩乎兩岸

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 門。閒田地上松風，田庫奴不知狼籍我多少？家無小廝，不成君子，簑衣箬笠，天晴時甚人曬㫰？斷頭船子下揚州，洪浪巨濤裏看風使帆，阿誰識得？李三黑一生只賣炭，雖然汙我清白家聲，泠地裏全承渠力，年來失錢遭罪，也須大家著隻眼。法堂草深丈許，我總不憂，秪憂太陽溢目，萬里不掛片雲，青天也須喫棒。時有目者不見，忽然南山起雲、北山下雨，溪深杓柄長，如何去取？三伏毒熱，井底冰生，鑊湯爐炭裏安居底，阿師還曾念我？赤骨律寒毛卓豎，俯仰乾坤無可告語，有懷如許，不審立業成家者作何料理？」「貧無卓錐，動容揚古路；富有四海，遍界不能藏。既藏不得，則從日炙風吹，隨波逐浪，或截流而渡，夾岸鳴榔；或深入不毛，千江釣雪。布帆明月，贏得夢貼蘆花；起倒黑甜，忘卻故鄉水草。無位真人行一步，過無量恒沙世界，未出渠儂毛孔；舒一光，蔽百千日月朗耀，不得其門而入。璣上座今日將其門洞啟，直令渠全身出現，普使群生萬有眼見耳聞、舌嘗鼻嗅、身觸意思，縱饒六根不具、八識不全者，一點也背渠不得。東山門下繇來火烈風嚴，間不容髮，而今覿面提持，如何迴避？若也避得，莫謂天台路嶮巇，羊腸更在青霄上；若避不得，相見易為好，共住難為情。」「家貧猶自可，路貧愁殺人。水不洗水，金不博金。江南塞北，月泠風高；東魯西秦，山深水闊。四衢道上磚，片片皆硬，開口告人難；大千沙界草，莖莖是藥，把手將不去，寒暑迭遷。解忌口者，一牛飲水，五馬不嘶；不解忌口者，求生不得，求死不得。未審我無上醫王，如何救療？」「昔日世尊，於涅槃會上，普告眾曰：『吾有正法眼藏，涅槃妙心，付囑摩訶迦葉。』若論正法眼藏，人人取之不竭，用之無窮，大千世界，無絲毫許障隔。涅槃妙心，圓明清淨，應物現形，放之則彌漫八極，卷之則匿跡韜光，在聖不增，處凡不減，因甚又道付囑摩訶迦葉？」「車不橫推，理無曲斷，雖則法爾如然，其奈絃急則促。文殊、普賢各各翻轉面皮，主人公二俱不受，情與無情，異口同音，曰：『官不容針，私通車馬。』觀音大士從聞、思、修入三摩地，曰：『某甲罪過。』長汀子於十字街頭呵呵大笑，曰：『口秪堪喫飯。』是則固是，忽有人拈起一粒，問云：『這箇從甚處得來？』又作麼生？」「好雨點點，不落在別處，無問情與無情，靡不承其恩力。其如根器匪一，弗克含藏，流而為泉、為澗、為沼、為池、為江漢、為河海，蹄涔溝澮無不有之，彼彼自深自滿，洋溢波濤，莫知源之所自。爰有一人截流而渡，指目彼岸此岸異派中流，既而舟航競作，往復無時，蕩蕩乎兩岸

Senses.Explanation: Water does not wash water; gold is not exchanged for gold. The pair uses sameness to challenge a search for an external purifier or separate equivalent. It is a teaching image, not a literal rule about washing or trade.

Senses.Explanation: To catch the moon in water is to grasp at a reflected appearance that cannot be seized there. Tianyin Yuanxiu says asserting that New Year's teaching exists is catching the moon in water. Chushi Fanqi asks how such catching could occur for one who tolerates no grit in the eye; Zhongfeng Mingben uses it in a verse on verbal learning; Ruibai Mingxue pairs it with trying to pluck a flower from a mirror. Zhuanyu Guanheng calls it wasted effort. Chan records retain the reflection scene and apply it to seeking the matter in an image, formulation, or opposed proposition.

Occurrences.Kwic: 密庵傑禪師奉聖旨就本寺開堂，上堂：靈源不昧，萬古徽猷，入此門來，莫存知解。知解既不生，如王寶劍，殺活臨時，舉一明三，目機銖兩，塵塵剎剎普現威權，物物頭頭全彰正眼，便見一塵含法界，一句截千差，於一毫端現寶王剎，坐微塵裏轉大法輪，高而無上，仰不可及，淵而無下，深不可測，自然風行草偃，水到渠成，不是神通妙用，亦非法爾如然。何故？乃是當人從無量劫來現成受用境界，契券分明，直饒千佛出現，各各放大寶光，也侵占一星兒不得。所以道：一切法不生，一切法不滅，若能如是解，佛法常現前。以此壽聖人，則天長地久；以此祝賢佐，則伊尹、周公；以此保國安民；以此康福天下。殊勝中殊勝，奇特中奇特，畢竟結角羅紋在什麼處？天上有星皆拱北，人間無水不朝東。復舉：僧問百丈大智禪師：如何是奇特事？百丈云：獨坐大雄峰。僧禮拜，百丈便打，師云：百丈善能據虎頭，亦能收虎尾，雖然頭尾兩全，至竟未徹源底。今日忽有問靈隱：如何是奇特事？只對他道：為國開堂。僧若禮拜，但云：知恩方解報恩。且道與百丈是同是別？若揀得出，平步青霄；其或未然，更聽一頌：虎驟龍驤與麼來，驀然平地起風雷，棒頭正眼明如日，凜凜清風廓九垓。久立眾慈，伏惟珍重。

Senses.Explanation: The proverb “when water arrives, the channel forms” (水到渠成) describes an outcome following when its conditions or accumulated work are already complete. Baiyun Shouduan asks why a great breakthrough is so and answers, “work accumulated, the undertaking completed; water arrives, the channel forms” (功多業就，水到渠成). Other hall addresses pair it with “the wind moves and the grass bends” (風行草偃), place it after “as a person reaches home,” or use it as the requested name of a sentence. The hydraulic sequence supplies the attested model: arrival and formation, without a separate forcing step.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Water flowing past stone comes out cool; wind passing through flowers comes fragrant

Senses.Note: Water cools as it flows by stone; wind comes fragrant through flowers. The pair makes a point through touch and smell, leaving the immediate scene to answer a question about what is present or how to recognize it. Fushi gives it after a question about an ancestral barrier; Hanyu asks why the immediately present is not accepted; other masters close sermons with it. The scene is concrete, and the surrounding question sets its force.

Senses.Explanation: A stream cools beside stone, and wind carries fragrance through flowers. Dabo closes a sermon with the pair, Fushi answers a barrier question with it, and Ruibai uses it at a retreat. Yun'e gives it after a case comment; Zixian ends a festival sermon with the same sensory pair. Hanyu asks why what is immediately present is not accepted, and Qiran gives the line after raising his staff.

AlternateTargets: The stream takes coolness from the rocks, and the breeze takes scent from the blossoms
SearchAliases: water by stone cool wind through flowers fragrant Chan
Senses.Note: Water emerges cool beside stone; wind arrives scented after passing through flowers. Poshan substitutes this pair for an older answer about ancestral and scriptural intent. Tianan uses it as a possible successful reply at a gate; Shaweng gives it in an exchange about a breeze, and Buhui closes his own question with it. Each scene shows a quality appearing through an encounter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 節兒孫在，萬壑千巖扇祖風。偃谿和尚至，上堂：同條不同條，心眼自相照。翻覆論歲寒，不覺拍手笑。且道笑箇甚麼？先師無板齒，眉毛只一莖。閏月十五清明，上堂：橫拄杖便與麼去，已落第二月，更說三年一閏。寒食是清明，轉見無交涉。喝一喝：達磨大師，當門齒缺。浴佛，上堂。一手指天，一手指地。釋迦老子飯飽弄筯，雲門一棒打殺。岳林今日澆惡水，大家輥入草窠裏。上堂，舉五祖演和尚道：有人向虗空中書得祖師西來意五字，老僧展坐具拜他。師云：岳林今日向弓弦上結紐。有个頌子：綠樹陰濃夏日長，樓臺倒影入池塘。水晶簾動微風起，滿架薔薇一院香。道場故舊到，上堂，舉光嚴童子問：維摩從何所來？士云：吾從道場來。子云：道場者何所？士云：直心是道場，無虗假故。乃至諸有所作，舉足下足皆是道場。師云：淨名探頭太過，忘却處所，縱懸河辯，去道轉遠。今日有人問：道場何所向？道：到江吳地盡，隔岸越山多。開神正閣󳬴，上堂。彈指樓閣門開，彌勒因正打邪。從門入已還閉，善財因邪打正。直得龍吟霧起，虎嘯風生。過去說，見在說，未來說，塵說，剎說，三世一時說。正與麼時，就中要覓一句子上󳬴，無有是處。喝一喝，文彩已彰。上堂：三到投子，九上洞山。窮廝

Senses.Explanation: The crystal curtain moves as a light breeze rises; roses fill the trellis and fragrance fills the courtyard. Answer with a full sensory scene that remains immediate rather than abstract. Feiyin Tongrong and Yunsou Benzhu use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Baiyu Jingsi, Dachuan Puji give further current deployments. This is the latter half of a secular summer poem actively reused in Chan records.

Senses.Explanation: The moon in water is the moon’s visible reflection on a water surface, not another moon that can be taken from the water. The Record of Xiangyan Xixin pictures the moon disk suspended in the blue sky and its round image falling into the ocean; the Records of the Source-Mirror describes the water-moon beside a mirror image and explicitly calls the constructed image provisional rather than real. Zhiyan Liaojue says that the bright moon casts its image over a clear pool while neither water nor moon intends the relation, and then speaks of forgetting both. Hongzhi’s verse retains the image as a moonlit waterscape. A previous temple-name substring has been removed because it names a place, not the reflection.

Entries.SourceTerm: 水歸大海波濤靜，雲到蒼梧氣象閒

Senses.PreferredTarget: Water returns to the great sea and its waves grow still; clouds reach Cangwu and the scene rests at ease.
AlternateTargets: Back in the ocean the waves are quiet; over Cangwu the clouds lie at ease.
Senses.Note: A paired image of settling into place. Cangwu is a named mountain region in the verse; the image serves as a closing answer to Chan questions about recognition or release.

Senses.Explanation: Water returns to the great sea and the waves settle; clouds reach Cangwu and the atmosphere becomes calm. The two lines image movement coming to rest. Hanxiu closes a Deshan case comment with the pair. Shiqi applies it after speaking about the unranked true person. Yune offers it as an answer about finally settling the matter. Shipu uses it to finish an inaugural hall question; Huanzhu gives it after asking about freedom from fetters. The image settles these turns without prescribing literal travel.

Senses.PreferredTarget: sealed so tight not even water passes
Senses.Note: No distinct literal-object sense was found for the exact four-character phrase in the sampled Zen evidence; the seal image and its transferred gate/command use form one idiomatic sense. The corpus itself supplies contrasts with “the ten directions unobstructed” and “wind passes and grass bends.”

SearchAliases: sealed so tight not even water passes
Zen sealed so tight not even water passes
Senses.Explanation: The phrase is attested. In the records it regularly describes the impassability of the ancestral gate and places associated with Bodhidharma: "before Shaoshi Peak, not even water passes" (少室峰前，水泄不通) and "under the patriarch's gate, not even water passes" (祖師門下，水泄不通). One address sets it against "the Buddha-work gate, where wind passes and grass bends" (佛事門中，風行草偃). Another makes it one of three eyes: one is watertight and ordinary and initiated cannot be distinguished; one opens the whole earth and the ten directions are unobstructed; one surveys high and low and all kinds look up. The phrase also enters public questioning: "where not even water passes, is there still a way through?" (水泄不通處還有過也無). Thus an ordinary image of a perfect seal becomes a stock Chan description of a gate, peak, command, or point at which passage is challenged.

Senses.Explanation: The water is shallow and there are no fish, so lowering the hook is wasted labor. Shaoshan Huanpu says it when Jingqing Daofu asks why he will not serve as a mirror after their extended contest of host and guest. The original exchange ends with Jingqing unable to answer and Shaoshan striking him; the Separate Transmission Outside the Teaching and the Empty Valley Collection raise the whole encounter and retain Shaoshan's answer. Panshan Liaozong reuses the same line directly in answer to a request for instruction, so the fishing image also functions outside the transmitted Shaoshan case.

Senses.Explanation: As the water rises, the boat rides higher; with more clay, the Buddha image grows larger. Show a response or achievement growing with its conditions. Baichi Xingyuan and Yinyuan Longqi use the complete saying in distinct recorded teaching turns. Guxue Zhenzhe, Yezhu Fuhui, and Shenfeng Xian give further current deployments. The parallel images describe dependence on conditions, not automatic spiritual progress.

Senses.Explanation: A water buffalo passes through a lattice window: its head, horns, and four hooves pass, but its tail does not. Wuzu Fayan states the image as a public question and makes the smallest remainder the obstruction: why does the tail fail when the large body has passed? Feiyin Tongrong and Miyin Zhenchuan preserve and raise that same attributed saying. An unnamed questioner in Shanduo Zhenzai’s record puts the case directly to him; Shanduo answers with rootless grass growing from stone and unmoving clouds held by a mountain. The answer is stored as the encounter’s response, not substituted into the headword’s gloss. Zen bends an impossible spatial picture into a repeatable question whose force lies in the unresolved remainder. The witnesses do not authorize reducing the case to a general slogan about being nearly complete.

Occurrences.Kwic: 者一念普觀無量劫，法昌只具一隻眼，只知有當日事，不知有今日事。如何是今日事？清風生八極，老虎出南山。上堂：居一切時不起妄念，於諸妄心亦不息滅，輕似鴻毛重似山。住妄想境不加了知，於無了知不辨真實，揑不成團擘不開。靈山節外生枝，報恩依文解義。諸人還知落處麼？自是不歸歸便得，五湖風月有誰爭？佛心禪師忌日，拈香。白鶴五通賢聖，瞥喜瞥嗔無定。聞名不如見面，見面依然錯認。從來與渠水米無交，年年今日鉢盂安柄。因甚如此？雞不喫糓，肫裏有病。開爐，上堂。地爐無火，事在莫嫌遲。冷灰豆𪹼，放過則不可。四藤條，五火杪，三十棒，古人都用了。且聽天寧倒行摩竭令。卓拄杖一下。上堂：毗婆尸佛早留心，直至如今不得妙。又道：妙高峰頂善財，七日不見德雲比丘。又道：文殊、普賢昨夜起佛見、法見，貶向二鐵圍山。此三段義是同是別？有時輥入洪波裏，盡日漫天皷黑風。上堂。西來無意，遍天遍
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1369.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dachuan Puji. Dachuan voices the no-water-or-rice idiom in his own incense offering on Buddha Mind masters memorial day.

SearchAliases: without exchanging even water or rice
Senses.Explanation: No exchange even of water or rice expresses a lack of ordinary dealings or dependence. Hanyue Fazang applies it to unbound practice; Yuanan Liao says a practitioner has no dealings with Shakyamuni or Bodhidharma. Muchen Daomin asks why an assembly quarrels with him despite no such dealings. Dachuan Puji voices it in his own memorial incense offering. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Explanation: By the water, beneath the trees — the hermit ground the tradition names in four graphs, where the holy embryo is nursed, the finished traveler rests, and, in one warning, the idler hides. Dufeng Shan's open talk to the assembly: when you finally find your entry point, do not rush off playing hollow tricks as a teacher, misleading yourself and others — copy the ancients: go first to the water's edge beneath the trees, nurse the holy embryo, and wait for the dragons and heavens to push you forth; only then teach; Liangting Jingting, instructing the ailing layman through the oxherding image: after the ancients got their hand they nursed the holy embryo by the water and trees, or walked among other kinds, entering water and mud, free and at ease — principle needs sudden awakening, affairs are shed stepwise; forty years beaten into one, apart from the two porridge-times no other use of mind; and Yingshan Zhiyin, in his night-talk warnings: the ancients ate from the broken-legged pot and went to the water's edge beneath the trees to nurse the holy embryo — that is the business after certainty — one must first smash through once, standing between heaven and earth, to wrest the scales from the patriarchs and buddhas and be eyes for humans and gods. Yezhu Fuhui: walking a step where patriarchs and buddhas cannot walk, speaking a word where they cannot speak — now that walking and speaking are both arrived at, not only howling at the moon on the lonely peak or the silk-and-pipe of the hot marketplace — just right, by the water beneath the trees, in hamlet and town-wall, go thus; Tianyin Yuanxiu, after appraising Sengzhao's root-and-body saying, snaps: on the patch-robed one's ledger, what then? — one bowl of a thousand households, idle by the water beneath the trees; Sanyi Mingyu, invited to Roar Mountain, sings himself: enough, enough — forty-odd years and the head already white; the torn robe outdoes heavy furs; wherever the water's edge beneath the trees gives ease, take your ease — few meet the blue-eyed gaze, the white eye laughs at lords; and Tianran Hanshi, hall talk: one two three, four five six — by the water beneath the trees, a thousand feet's worth, ten-thousand feet' worth; one tumble and the green-yellow-red shows — only beware colliding with Meng the Eighth, who'll whack your donkey's head with a crack; why? In the black-lacquered dish, wheat and beans are not told apart. And the warning: Wuyi Yuanlai's admonitions describe the man whose doubt will not fire, who wants to go loose and lively, singing and dancing for whoever comes, or laughing and chatting by the water beneath the trees, or swaggering through the market lanes, calling himself a finished man — who sees a knowing teacher open a monastery and set the rules and claps his hands and laughs with scorn; the admonition keeps the place honest: without the doubt fired, the water's edge is only scenery.

Senses.Explanation: As the water rises, the boat rises; as the clay increases, the Buddha image grows. The paired images speak of function or form growing with conditions. Current deployments include Liangting Jingting in J33nB294, Pinjixiang Zhixiang in J39nB454, and Yanju Deshen in J40nB478. Baoning Renyong in X69n1350 provides a fourth current hall use. The full paired image remains the lexical unit. The clay-Buddha image need not mean spiritual rank grows automatically with material abundance.

Senses.Explanation: The Land of Bliss soundscape — water-birds and tree-groves — ruled at the root over Dongshan's insentient-preaching question, then roared from staff-heads, sheared from litanies, and swapped for eyes across nine centuries of halls and odes. The root sits in Yunyan Tansheng's own answer, carried in the true-eye storehouse: Dongshan asks what canonical teaching the insentient preaching belongs to, and Yunyan answers: do you not see the Amitabha sutra — water-birds and tree-groves, all of them minding the buddha, minding the teaching; the insentient grasses and trees playing reed-pipes to each other — and Dongshan woke partway there, oding: how utterly strange, the insentient preaching unthinkable; try to hear it with the ear and it will never meet you — sound known at the eye is the only way; Huangbo Xiyun, in the Wanling record, folds it into the never-silent: speech is silence, silence is speech, the sound's own true nature never cut off; the thus-come always speaks, never a time of not-speaking — the teaching is the speaking, the speaking the teaching — down to the reward-body and the transformation-body, the voice-hearers, mountains and rivers, the great earth, water-birds and tree-groves, all preaching at once: speaking in speech and speaking in silence, all day speaking and never once having spoken — and so, take silence for the root; Baiyun Shouduan, in the five-house praises: as I press my finger, the ocean-seal gives off its light — the staff lifted, and mountains, rivers, the great earth, water-birds and tree-groves, the sentient and the insentient, all making the great lion's roar atop the staff-head, preaching the great perfection of wisdom; and Xiaoyin Daxin, at the great report-lands temple, sets the two lands against each other — the Land of Bliss, where water-birds and tree-groves all mind the buddha; the Contentment heaven, where trees brushing together preach the bitter and the empty — then the whisk raised: this mountain monk's whisk threads your nostrils — where will you breathe out? Tianyin Yuanxiu, oding the very question Dongshan asked: water-birds and tree-groves all mind the teaching — what sentient being cannot hear it and understand?; sunk through ten thousand kalpas and suddenly awake: every thing, every head, always already complete; Shanhui Huan shears the litany apart — seal mind with mind and mind has no such mind; hand the teaching on and the teaching has no such teaching: mountains and rivers are their own mountains and rivers, the ten thousand forms their own ten thousand forms, water-birds and tree-groves their own water-birds and tree-groves, the sage-and-commoner measure its own measure, fine words their own fine words, staff and shout their own staff and shout — the whole heap of them nothing to do with me — and the staff knocks once: the yaksha draws its sword and stirs the dragon-gate, a thousand fathoms, ten thousand fathoms, shaking the sea; and Shiyu Mingfang, at the Baoshou hall: before you stepped over the boat's gunwale, one Baoshou had already been inscribed on your mind-source; all the way here — dressing, eating, talking, laughing — each a single Baoshou, not high, not low, not big, not small; and then on arrival, the water-birds and tree-groves, the bells, chimes, gongs and drums went and swapped your eyes; they never left Baoshou — but can you hear the water-birds and tree-groves all minding buddha, minding teaching, minding the order?; the old worthies' line — with the ear you will never meet it; known in the eye at last — so tell me: how does the eye hear? how does the eye see?

Occurrences.Kwic: 穢，入佛入不得魔，入順入不得逆，便有人境之分，限量之隔。何故？是他見識不忘，氣質未化，被人一折，便生嗔恨。若不一刀兩段，大有事在。又屢承師友錐劄，又恐見諦不實，難逃順逆二境，奔馳南北，借是非場、假利害劍，磨煉習態，方得疑情頓脫、見惑銷融，外無他求、內無所守，纔見達磨直指之道，不費絲毫氣力。僧已年暮，精神漸減，難奉人情，只好歸山，放闊空懷，渴飲饑餐，閒遊倦眠，只待瓜熟蒂落，大寂光中作個滿散矣。復梅司馬衡湘復梅司馬衡湘臺下靈州之役，其作用妙處，與卓老談之久矣。嗣後聞拂衣之說，豈有他哉？蓋謂生死難明，欲于風波中求出頭耳。夫道本無方，迷於執方，丈夫事業無妨道也。不曰不離法場而證菩提乎？然未可謂功業真無妨道也，不有捨淨飯之位而入雪山者乎？要之，隱現無所不可，惟不辦生死之心，徒爾效顰，則真不可耳。令愛真靈照復出，不知若翁果龐居士否？居士沉金帛于水矣，若翁獨不能沉功業於水乎？又接手書，感承遠教所云世緣素輕近益脫

Occurrences.Kwic: 渡水登山便恁麼去。家裏人逢家裏言，抽釘拔楔誠良御。誠良御，休落草，等閒更莫打之遶。春水揚帆歸及早，缽囊待爾來收好。送鑑藏主還嘉禾送鑑藏主還嘉禾通身只個大圓鏡，萬象森羅一印印，白蘋紅蓼滿汀洲，目底閒閒秋水浚。青山不敢青、白雲不敢白，一大藏教明歷歷。歸去來，歸去來，悠悠伴我空崔嵬。送恂知客還白下送恂知客還白下朴實頭禪只一句，盡在尋常行履處。渴飲饑餐不等閒，閒閒豈可為活計？江南江北任縱橫，足底從來坦坦平，賓主相逢休話墮，臨機貴要忘其情。秋風涼，秋路長，石頭城去一千五百里，白雲盡處山蒼蒼。送介嵩上人送介嵩上人高高山頂立，清風生八極，深深海底行，步步起紅塵。有力者，剔起眉毛便去，吳山越水任爾縱橫。力不足者，腳頭腳底切莫因循。達磨西來，文字不立，直指人心，見性成佛，冷坐九年嵩山面壁。可大師，庭前立，斷臂覓心不可得，一言之下便寧帖。帖帖帖休述，彼既丈夫我亦爾，那個男兒不如此？上人之號號介嵩，介嵩之介介何窮？直須窮徹無窮底，踢出須彌第一峰。

Senses.Explanation: To break a precept is to violate a binding rule. Fayan Wenyi cites the code's own ruling that deliberately hearing ornaments through a wall counts as violation, then turns it into a question in the hall. In Zhongshan Daoquan's Zutang Ji case, an unnamed monk raises the sharper formula that a precept-breaking monk does not fall into hell, while Yulin Tongxiu says one who breaks the precepts is no different from wood. Baizhang Huaihai extends the charge to seeking for mind, calling every such seeker a precept-breaking monk. Muchen Daomin says that only a buddha keeps the pure precept and all others are breakers. Yongming Yanshou quotes the instruction not to look for violation in another person's body. The corpus therefore keeps the concrete category of violation while testing where the breach is located and whether outward judgment has reached it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 禪師重慶何氏子。上堂，舉：教中道：若見諸相非相，即見如來。作麼生是非相底道理？佯走詐羞偷眼󳬇，竹門斜掩半枝花。五燈全書卷第四十六五燈全書卷第四十七京都聖感禪寺住持僧編輯京都古華嚴寺住持僧較閱進呈臨濟宗南嶽下十七世南嶽下十七世天童華禪師法嗣天童華禪師法嗣慶元府天童密菴咸傑禪師慶元府天童密菴咸傑禪師福州鄭氏子。母夢廬山老僧入舍而生。自幼穎悟，出家不憚遊行，徧參知識。後謁應菴於明果，菴孤硬難入，屢遭呵。一日入室，菴問：如何是正法眼？師遽答曰：破沙盆。菴頷之。及辭回省親，菴送以偈曰：大徹投機句，當陽廓頂門。相從今四載，徵詰洞無痕。雖未付鉢袋，氣宇吞乾坤。却把正法眼，喚作破沙盆。此行將省覲，切忌便跺跟。吾有末後句，待歸要汝遵。出世衢之烏巨，次遷祥符、蔣山、華藏。未幾，詔住徑山，復遷靈隱，晚居太白。上堂：佛說一切法，為度一切心。我無一切心，何用一切法？既無心，又無法，山河大地甚處得來？見聞覺知復是何物？乃喝一喝，曰：臨崖看滸眼，特地一場愁。上堂：一進一退，一動一靜，須信那伽常在定。一擒

Senses.Explanation: Worn-out straw sandals are damaged travel footwear fit to discard; Chan speakers make the contemptuous object an answer or comparison for formulations, accomplishments, and lineage emblems that someone is still carrying. Huangbo Xiyun calls the patriarchs' dark purport worn-out straw sandals; Jiashan Shanhui answers 'What is the Way?' with them and says to throw them into the lake. Bajiao Huiqing locates a pair inside the house, Foguo asks what they are worth after the matter is understood, Weian Deran calls even seeing the morning star street-side worn-out sandals, and Wuchu Daguan has half a soleless sandal. These are uses of the bare worn-out-sandals headword; the different wear-out-the-sandals predicate is routed to family evidence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 非聖亦非凡，無外亦無內。我此一片香，供養法中王，靈根盤劫外，遍界不曾藏。師年九十九，未出剎那際。木馬驟清風，泥牛耕實地。劫外自高歌，幻海恣遊戲。癡兒不解事，歲歲空相憶。一盃清茗一爐香，萬古千秋只如是。金鷄呌出三更月，百歲兒童頭似雪，今日親從那畔來，描不成兮畵不得。既來，為甚麼描畵不得？良久，云：刀斧砍不開，相見不相識。丁酉與辛酉，五五二十五。岸行舟不行，木人撾石鼓。大眾，還見老和尚藏身處麼？日出啣山，月圓當戶。寶福山中逢忌，燒香恰熏著鼻，兩孔襲襲生煙，直得通天徹地，惟有一處熏不著。且道是那一處？良久，云：莫言老漢不慈悲，諸佛從來不出位。生之年，死之日，打破虗空尋鳥迹。大眾還見老和尚麼？熱似月兮冷如日。年年此日修歸忌，勿問吾師來不來。但看深山十月菊，家家都向此時開。掃塔掃塔違師不覺忽三年，休咎疾疴常示夢。我心師心同一體，此恩何啻丘山重。一片旃檀爇塔前，夢中驚破玉人眠。吾師說法原無間，試聽雷音震大千。百歲慶忌掃塔百歲慶忌掃塔百年三萬六千日，日日分明一百年，經歷百千無量劫，吾師壽量未曾遷。一縷檀雲籠塔頂，半輪秋月掛峯巔，當機覿面無回互，萬古江山在目前。頌頌舉華嚴行願品云：一切如來有長子，彼名號曰普賢尊，我今迴向諸善根，願諸智行悉同彼。頌曰：塵剎如來之長子，克擔家法曰普賢。願周法界真因滿，德遍塵方覺果圓。位後位前同一
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1442.xml). Drafts from Chan Master Weilin’s Traveling Hermitage. The complete case names Weilin Daopei as the speaker of the headword-bearing wording.

Occurrences.Kwic: 童親口道，不萌枝上辨春秋，無影波中紅日杲，黧奴白牯却知有，出門有路落荒草。今日乃元旦啟祚之辰，老僧特為陞座祝延聖壽，即今報恩護國一句作麼生道？金輪永鎮三千界，寶籙長延億萬年。恒如老友請示眾。老僧昔年與恒如老友同入博山社火，其時博山老人祇以一口氣不來向甚麼處去話鈍置天下人，至今二十五年矣。今日恒如特登山見訪，不免重拈舊話報博山恩去也。生從何來？鐵鋸舞三臺；死從何去？三臺吞鐵鋸。勿以明相覩，勿以暗相遇，坐斷兩頭關，銀花開鐵樹。堪咲當年博山老不解放行，祇解把住老僧今日放行去也。諸人還會麼？咦！夜半石人方反側，一場好夢向誰言？我聞老宿入塔請示眾：枯木裏有龍吟，吼破虗空不露身；髑髏裏有眼睛，炤徹乾坤不見塵。今日收歸無縫塔，大悲手眼莫能尋。諸人還識得無縫塔麼？昔唐肅宗問忠國師云：百年後所須何物？師資分上，仁義道中。國師云：為我造一無縫塔，婆心太切，亦是老不知休。肅宗云：請師塔樣作家君王。國師良久云：會麼？無言可對，無理可伸，這裏活陷多少人？肅宗不會，到底作家。國師云：吾有得法弟子躭源，可詔問之，推禍離身。遷化後，詔問躭源：國師意旨如何？向餬餅裏討汁。躭源頌云：湘之南，潭之北，畢竟是甚麼所在？中有黃金充一國。失却了也，無影樹下合同船；切莫認著，琉璃殿上無知識。要有作麼？今日老僧將無縫塔重重托出了也。如其未會，老僧再為註破。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1437.xml). Expanded Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian. The complete case names Yongjue Yuanxian as the speaker of the headword-bearing wording.

Occurrences.Kwic: 山僧今日為上官司戶陞座舉揚與他下箇注脚生耶死耶通徹不道不道直截一鎚打破虗空當下七花八烈。

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：一滴水，一滴凍，喝下風雷彰大用。棒頭點出眼睛來，照了諸相悉空洞。出門撞著須菩提，拶破虗空全體露。

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: ，南北東西成隊走。塞破虗空一窖無，傾出神珠三百
ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 。巍巍堂堂是什麼，壁立萬仞如懸崖。諸方既火葬，我此但活埋。當頭一坐斷，豈受人差排。神通光明藏，受用俱偶諧。滿禪如此窮教徹，此是休居真實說。送覺首座遊京都送覺首座遊京都去去實不去，楖栗一條生鐵鑄；來來實不來，門前古路生蒼苔。煙塵漠漠幾千里，白日照曜黃金臺。頂門眼既正，人我山當摧，一舉四十九，揑聚還放開。所以佛祖機，不著言語該，風行即艸偃，處處興雲雷。丈夫行脚有如此，燕南冀北誠悠哉！使夫德山、臨濟聞而歡喜、見而贊嘆，是謂法王之真子，可以展三玄戈甲、列五位君臣，大張爐鞴之才，天上人間不可陪。咄！咄！送珍藏主遊西湖送珍藏主遊西湖天何高，地何厚，南北東西成隊走。塞破虗空一窖無，傾出神珠三百斗。取也不在進前，捨也不在落後。一物不將來，誰道空雙手。丹桂飄香十里湖，小艇輕舠賣菱藕。送權禪人參東禪送權禪人參東禪權衡祖道無今古，四七二三難比數。忽然突出三脚驢，踏碎虗空無寸土。眼上眉毛雙卓竪，傾出黃河清到底。少待與汝都揭翻，洗光佛日誠不難。善用其心於一切處，佛祖難窺，人天罔措。大千沙界沒絲毫，八萬四千風過耳。全暗即全明，法爾渾不爾。跣足肩擔走不休，擡頭撞著自家底。阿呵呵，古往今來爭奈何。送宗知客送宗知客天無門，地無戶，南北東西有何數？一句臨機萬仞崖，三玄指出千差路。草底捉飛鷹，樹頭走凉兔，水上輥蓬塵，大地無寸土。相喚相呼去喫茶，記
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1413.xml). Supplementary Gathas and Verses of Chan Master Gulin Qingmao. The complete case names Gulin Qingmao as the speaker of the headword-bearing wording.

Senses.Explanation: Breaking, piercing, or bursting empty space marks an impossible scale of penetration or release. The retained poems and addresses use the image for a breakthrough that leaves no ordinary boundary intact, while the two recorded-sayings witnesses preserve direct instructional uses.

Entries.SourceTerm: 破鏡不重照，落花難上枝

Senses.PreferredTarget: a broken mirror does not reflect again, and a fallen flower cannot return to the branch

Senses.Explanation: A broken mirror will not shine again, and a fallen blossom cannot climb back to its branch. Foyuan uses the pair in a current sermon on passing time; Huaihai makes it the opening of an original verse on the Buddha case; Liaoan gives it as a direct answer to a question about transmission. The three prior witnesses remain as separate uses, including the useful early lamp. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Explanation: Breaking into a smile is Kashyapa's recorded response when Shakyamuni Buddha raises a flower before the assembly. In the Chan record the action is not a settled badge of approval: masters repeatedly raise the same scene and then praise, question, or attack the reported exchange. Wanru Tongwei and Dahui Zonggao contrast Kashyapa's smile with the assembly's failure to respond; both place the reported charge immediately afterward. Yuansou Xingduan retells exactly that sequence and caps it with ‘one blind person leads a crowd of blind people’ (一盲引眾盲), while Juelang Daosheng asks whether the eye reportedly handed over was originally present or absent. The stable fact is the case action and its place in the exchange; the later verdicts do not supply a second meaning of the phrase.
